sources.title: Stephen P. Martin, A Supersymmetry Primer, version 7
sources.locator: §3.1 (printed pp. 18–21); §3.2 (printed pp. 22–24); §§4.1–4.2 (printed pp. 31–34); §4.5 (printed pp. 38–39); §4.7 (printed pp. 41–42); §§4.8–4.9 (printed pp. 43–48). The 160-page PDF was retrieved and the listed sections were read in full.

source_review.read_extent: §3.1 covers the free chiral multiplet with its auxiliary field; §3.2 gives polynomial superpotential interactions and F elimination; §4.7 reconstructs the chiral action in superspace.
source_review.supports: The classical Wess–Zumino field content, superspace action, and canonical chiral auxiliary sector.
source_review.limitations: The source uses its own component normalizations. The carrier states the workspace sigma/Grassmann conventions and includes a positive general Kähler metric explicitly. No quantum continuum construction is inferred.

contents.name: The classical Wess–Zumino field content, superspace action, and canonical chiral auxiliary sector.

source_review.read_extent: §3.1 reads the auxiliary-field off-shell closure argument; §§4.1–4.2 read Berezin total derivatives and the superspace translation operator; §4.7 reads the D/F action construction.
source_review.supports: The independent chiral multiplet variation with F retained, and the superspace total-derivative route for the action.
source_review.limitations: The local proof derives the exact operator identity and compact-support boundary conclusion in the declared conventions; Martin's component normalization is not copied as a premise.

contents.name: The independent chiral multiplet variation with F retained, and the superspace total-derivative route for the action.

source_review.read_extent: §3.2 reads the full algebraic elimination of F for a canonical chiral metric and the resulting sum-of-squares potential.
source_review.supports: For canonical Kähler metric, eliminating F gives a nonnegative potential equal to the squared norm of the holomorphic superpotential gradient.
source_review.limitations: The carrier proves the inverse-metric formula for a general positive Kähler metric by completing the Hermitian square; it does not apply the canonical sum unchanged to noncanonical metrics.

contents.name: For canonical Kähler metric, eliminating F gives a nonnegative potential equal to the squared norm of the holomorphic superpotential gradient.

source_review.read_extent: §4.5 reads the real vector-superfield definition, component content, Wess–Zumino gauge, and its failure to be preserved by an uncompensated supersymmetry variation; §4.9 reads the non-Abelian field-strength construction.
source_review.supports: A real vector prepotential with gauge boson, gaugino, auxiliary component, and the non-Abelian chiral field-strength construction.
source_review.limitations: The local definition fixes Hermitian SU(2) generators and the workspace connection normalization explicitly; no global gauge fixing is asserted.

contents.name: A real vector prepotential with gauge boson, gaugino, auxiliary component, and the non-Abelian chiral field-strength construction.

source_review.read_extent: §4.9 reads the representation-valued matter D-term, supergauge law, and non-Abelian field-strength action; §4.8 reads the coupling and kinetic normalization context.
source_review.supports: The gauge-covariant chiral matter action, representation matrices, and common gauge coupling in the superspace formulation.
source_review.limitations: The external text's trace and metric normalizations differ. The local postulate sets SU(2), kappa=-2 Tr_2, eta=(-+++), and the exact match to the supplied pure Yang–Mills curvature term.

contents.name: The gauge-covariant chiral matter action, representation matrices, and common gauge coupling in the superspace formulation.

source_review.read_extent: §4.2 reads superspace transformations as translations; §4.9 reads the full non-Abelian gauge-matter D/F action structure.
source_review.supports: Full-superspace D-terms and chiral F-terms as the standard manifestly supersymmetric action construction.
source_review.limitations: The proof is local for the full prepotential and compact-support boundary condition. It does not establish gauge-anomaly cancellation or supersymmetry in a gauge-fixed Wess–Zumino representative.

contents.name: Full-superspace D-terms and chiral F-terms as the standard manifestly supersymmetric action construction.

source_review.read_extent: §3.2 reads the polynomial superpotential expansion and auxiliary equation for the canonical one-field example.
source_review.supports: The cubic one-field superpotential and its local F-term potential structure.
source_review.limitations: The example differentiates its own polynomial and substitutes the local theorem; no numerical or empirical claim is imported.

contents.name: The cubic one-field superpotential and its local F-term potential structure.

source_review.read_extent: §4.9 reads the general representation-valued gauge covariant derivative and matter D-term.
source_review.supports: Context for chiral matter in a finite-dimensional gauge representation.
source_review.limitations: The explicit fundamental SU(2) matrix multiplication and transition-covariance calculation are derived locally.

contents.name: Context for chiral matter in a finite-dimensional gauge representation.
contents.reason: Included only for the source’s recorded representation-valued gauge derivative and matter D-term conventions. The fundamental SU(2) matrix expansion and transition-covariance calculation remain the local example’s own calculation, not a result attributed to Martin.
